episode.title: [Linux Desktop] local stdio MCP launch inherits unrelated app-server file descriptors into MCP servers and their children
episode.before: The local Unix stdio launcher constructed a child command with piped stdin/stdout/stderr and a new process group, but did not set a descriptor-inheritance policy. The shared command builder therefore retained its default DescriptorPolicy::Inherit, allowing inheritable, unrelated descriptors held by the orchestrator to reach the local MCP server and any descendants it launched. The local runtime path selected LocalStdioServerLauncher for local stdio MCP configurations and passed that command through RmcpClient to the launcher.
episode.after: The local Unix stdio launcher sets DescriptorPolicy::StdioOnly on every locally constructed MCP command. The existing Unix spawn backend then closes inheritable descriptors other than the explicit transport stdio before exec, while retaining the internal exec-error reporting path; the macOS native backend uses its close-on-exec-default path. The server and descendants therefore inherit only the explicitly wired stdio transport, while the existing process group, arguments, environment, working directory, MCP protocol exchange, and launch-error behavior remain intact. The change is guarded by cfg(unix); Windows behavior is intentionally unchanged and remains a deferred handle-allowlist concern.
episode.diff: Commit afe4249cfe, parent b4b30dd5eb9994ddc51f915ecd74e9a8c1d93248, modifies codex-rs/rmcp-client/src/stdio_server_launcher.rs by adding Unix DescriptorPolicy support and applying command.descriptor_policy(DescriptorPolicy::StdioOnly) inside the local command builder. It adds codex-rs/rmcp-client/tests/stdio_descriptor_boundary.rs, a Unix-only integration test that creates inheritable pipe, socket, and file descriptors, verifies an unfiltered control launch sees them, then exercises absolute, relative, and shell-fallback local launches and asserts that neither the MCP server nor its descendant sees them. The test also checks MCP communication, arguments, environment, working directory, stderr, parent descriptor ownership after shutdown, and direct exec-failure reporting. No shared descriptor backend, remote executor path, or Windows implementation is changed.

evidence_units.claim: The pinned commit is titled “Restrict Unix local MCP servers to stdio descriptors (#47094)” and its commit message states that unrelated parent file descriptors should not propagate into local MCP servers or their descendants; it describes applying DescriptorPolicy::StdioOnly and adding Unix integration tests.
The commit changes exactly one launcher implementation file and adds one integration-test file: the launcher receives 9 inserted lines and the new test contains 231 inserted lines.
evidence_units.source: git diff --stat and git show --name-status b4b30dd5eb9994ddc51f915ecd74e9a8c1d93248 afe4249cfe

evidence_units.claim: Before the change, LocalStdioServerLauncher::launch_server built a Command, applied current_dir, environment, arguments, and ProcessMode::NewGroup, and then returned the command without setting descriptor_policy; the parent version therefore relied on Command's default descriptor policy.

At the pinned ref, stdio_server_launcher.rs imports DescriptorPolicy only under cfg(unix) and applies command.descriptor_policy(DescriptorPolicy::StdioOnly) immediately after setting ProcessMode::NewGroup. The adjacent implementation comment states that unrelated orchestrator descriptors must not propagate into the server or commands it launches and that Windows still needs a separate handle allowlist.

The shared Command type defaults to DescriptorPolicy::Inherit; its Unix StdioOnly path installs pre-exec cleanup that closes inherited descriptors other than standard descriptors while preserving close-on-exec descriptors used for spawn-error reporting. The macOS native path maps StdioOnly to POSIX_SPAWN_CLOEXEC_DEFAULT.

The production MCP setup selects LocalStdioServerLauncher for local McpServerTransportConfig::Stdio configurations and passes it to RmcpClient::new_stdio_client_with_protocol_mode; non-local configurations use the executor-backed launcher instead.

RmcpClient packages the program, arguments, environment, environment variables, cwd, and protocol mode into StdioServerCommand and dispatches the command through launcher.launch(command.clone()), so the local launcher policy is on the actual stdio process-creation path.

The new Unix integration test creates inheritable duplicates of a pipe, Unix socket, and file descriptor. A control process launched without the MCP descriptor policy must observe all three sentinels as present, establishing that the fixture can detect inheritance.

The same integration test runs local MCP launches through absolute, relative, and shell-fallback command forms, initializes the MCP connection, lists tools, calls the probe tool, and asserts that both the server and its descendant observe [false, false, false] for the pipe/socket/file sentinels while stdio round-trip, stderr, cwd, environment, argument handling, and request arguments remain correct.

After shutting down the MCP clients, the test reads the parent descriptors' F_GETFD flags and asserts they remain open and unchanged, proving descriptor cleanup is confined to the spawned process rather than mutating parent ownership.

A second Unix integration test creates an executable script whose interpreter is missing, then asserts that local stdio client creation returns an error; its comment specifically protects direct exec-failure reporting when descriptor cleanup is enabled.

The commit's Testing section identifies the intended validation scope: absence of inheritable pipe, socket, and file descriptors in servers and descendants across absolute, relative, and shell-fallback launches, plus preserved MCP communication, arguments, environment, working directory, parent descriptor ownership, and exec-failure reporting.
evidence_units.source: git show --format=fuller afe4249cfe, commit message Testing section

candidate_atomics.name: guard_local_unix_stdio_descriptor_boundary
candidate_atomics.description: Configure the local Unix stdio extension-process launch so unrelated descriptors inherited by the orchestrator do not cross into the extension server or its descendants, while the explicit stdio transport and existing launch settings remain usable.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent unrelated parent file descriptors from leaking into a local stdio extension process tree while preserving the explicit transport stdio.
semantic_action.pre_state: The local launch command has piped standard streams and a new process group but leaves descriptor policy at Inherit, so inheritable parent descriptors can be inherited by the server and by commands it launches.
semantic_action.post_state: On Unix, local stdio launches enforce a stdio-only inheritance boundary: the server and descendants inherit the explicit transport stdio but not unrelated inheritable parent descriptors, with existing arguments, environment, cwd, process-group, and exec-error behavior preserved.
semantic_action.validation: The added Unix integration oracle first proves that an unfiltered control launch sees the pipe, socket, and file sentinels, then verifies [false, false, false] in both the local server and a close_fds=False descendant across absolute, relative, and shell-fallback launches; it also checks MCP round-trip behavior, parent descriptor ownership, and failed-exec reporting.
parameters: unrelated inheritable pipe, socket, and file descriptors
Unix server and descendant process tree

candidate_atomics.name: validate_local_unix_stdio_boundary
candidate_atomics.description: Add an executable regression oracle for descriptor isolation and for the compatibility behaviors that must survive the new process boundary.

semantic_action.intent: Make the local Unix stdio descriptor invariant and its non-regression requirements directly testable.
semantic_action.module_role: Unix local stdio launch integration oracle
semantic_action.pre_state: The launch policy needs coverage proving both descriptor exclusion and preservation of protocol, argument, environment, cwd, parent-ownership, fallback, and exec-failure behavior.
semantic_action.post_state: The checked-in Unix tests distinguish an unfiltered launch from the policy-enabled launch and provide assertions for server/descendant exclusion and preserved behavior across all three launch forms.
semantic_action.validation: The integration tests assert control presence, policy-enabled absence, MCP initialize/list/call results, preserved stderr/cwd/environment/arguments, unchanged parent F_GETFD state, and an error for a missing interpreter.
parameters: absolute, relative, and shell-fallback launch forms

candidate_workflows.name: local_unix_stdio_descriptor_lifecycle
candidate_workflows.description: At the local stdio extension-process boundary, apply the Unix-only descriptor guard and then validate that the server tree receives only transport stdio without regressing communication, launch compatibility, parent ownership, or failure reporting.

workflow_graph.goal: Ensure local Unix stdio extension servers and their descendants cannot inherit unrelated orchestrator descriptors while the stdio transport and established launch contract remain functional.
workflow_graph.entry_state: A local stdio server is launched with the shared command's default inherited-descriptor policy, so unrelated inheritable descriptors may enter the server process tree and the regression boundary is not covered by an end-to-end oracle.
workflow_graph.exit_state: The local Unix launch path enforces stdio-only descriptor inheritance, server and descendant probes report no unrelated sentinels, and the integration oracle confirms MCP communication, launch variants, arguments, environment, cwd, parent descriptor ownership, and exec-failure reporting.
unresolved_or_deferred: The implementation is gated by cfg(unix); the commit explicitly leaves Windows unrelated-handle inheritance to a future shared-spawn handle allowlist, and the added integration test is Unix-only.
The issue bundle contains no issue body, comments, timeline, or linked pull-request metadata, so acceptance criteria beyond the local implementation and commit testing note are unavailable.

unresolved_questions: The issue bundle has no issue body, comments, timeline, or linked pull-request metadata; the implementation-bearing commit and checked-out tests are the available resolution evidence.

Windows local stdio handle filtering is explicitly outside this change: the launcher applies StdioOnly only on Unix, and the implementation comment says Windows still needs a handle allowlist in the shared spawn backend.

No fresh execution of the Unix-only integration test was performed during extraction, so validation is represented by the checked-in assertions and the commit's stated testing scope rather than a newly observed test result.
